name: Petal Unfurl
desc: A dense herbarium plate of flowers opening by differential growth rather than by keyframe — the adaxial surface outgrows the abaxial until each petal's curvature reverses through zero and the bud reflexes itself open, stamens tremble at anthesis, then turgor fails, the ribbons go slack and the petals abscise one by one to leave a bare receptacle for the next bud; sixteen blooms staggered across the sheet at depth, so something is always unfurling and something always shedding.

energy.doc: life-cycle rate + sway/tremble amplitude + petal flutter (master knob)

density.doc: how many blooms of the 16-flower pool are on the sheet (2 at 0 -> 14 at 1)

scale.doc: bloom size vs frame (0.35 = a scattered plate of small specimens, 2.2 = a single corolla fills the view)

hue.doc: corolla hue (wilt always drifts it warmer)

style.doc: aesthetic — botanical plate w/ ink line + stipple modelling; Atkins photogram on Prussian blue; additive translucent radiograph; form built from a single pool of light, no outline

seed.doc: seeds placement, view tilt, proportions and the petal-shedding order

alpha.doc: opacity of the flowers over the ground
